sources.role: Application identity, archive and manual links, documented survival significance issue.
Original Fortran routines and separate mathematical/user documentation; locally compiled numerical references. Original source and binaries are not bundled.
User manual, February 2010, including the one-sample normal power example (difference 1, SD 10, n 156, power 0.344).

implementation: Independent mathematical implementations. No original Fortran routine or manual text is incorporated in the package.

reference.reproduction: In an empty build directory, compile the listed original source files in order together with the repository harness, using the listed flags and -o reference_stplan. Run reference_stplan and capture stdout as the CSV fixture. The original archive must be acquired separately.

compatibility: Two-sided planning halves alpha and retains one rejection direction. Most procedures follow the alternative; case-control and historical-survival one-sided conventions preserve their documented fixed direction.
Correlation formulas follow current cor_nor_app_mod, pcor1 and pcor2, including the null SD for one-sample power.
Lognormal CV is SD/mean, consistent with qlgn2 and its formula.
Modern tail evaluation does not reproduce original quantile probability clamps.

discrete_reference.reproduction: In an empty build directory, compile the listed original source files in order together with this repository harness, using the listed flags and -o reference_stplan_discrete. Run the executable and capture stdout as the CSV fixture. The original archive must be acquired separately.
discrete_reference.empty_region: Two fixture rows retain the native -1 sentinel for an empty exact-test rejection region. Python intentionally returns the mathematically valid power 0 for these rows.

mixture_reference.reproduction: Compile the listed original source files in order with the repository harness in an empty build directory using the listed flags. Run the resulting executable and capture stdout as the native CSV fixture. Original source must be acquired separately.
mixture_reference.independent_runtime: R 4.4.1, base and stats packages only
mixture_reference.independent_method: Finite probability sums enumerate nonrandomized binomial rejection regions. Matched tests fix the upper-tail null at 0.5; Poisson tests mix over total events, with omitted reference mass below 1e-14.
native_defects: fmcaco passes case-only probability as the binomial null and 0.5 as its alternative, contrary to the intended null of 0.5.
ppoi2 uses a renormalized 99% Poisson sum, can duplicate integer modes, and substitutes a single test at the mean above 200 events.

survival_reference.reproduction: Compile the listed original source files in order with the repository harness in an empty build directory using the listed flags. Run the resulting executable and capture stdout as the native CSV fixture. Original source must be acquired separately.
survival_reference.independent_runtime: R 4.4.1, base and stats packages only
survival_reference.independent_method: Reads only the argument columns of native cases. Adaptive quadrature integrates uniform-accrual event probabilities, splitting at the piecewise hazard breakpoint. R distribution functions evaluate the planning formulas; a wide finite Poisson sum has omitted mass below 1e-14. Three additional R-only cases cover an interior hazard breakpoint and zero hazard in either segment.
native_differences: p1exp stops on small weighted contributions; the bounded Python Poisson sum instead controls omitted probability. Observed native difference from the independent reference is at most 8.6e-8.
prct2 uses original quantile solvers with approximately 1e-7 tolerance; observed reference differences are at most 1.1e-8.
pint2 and pschc match the independently computed normal approximations to floating-point rounding.
p2exp_mod fails to normalize survival integrals and can evaluate unclamped entry intervals. Two native cases produce NaN and the third differs from corrected quadrature.
The a2exp interface and p2exp_mod disagree about numeric model-arm labels. Python names the supplied lower- or higher-hazard arm explicitly.
The historical-control menu is one-sided. Python sides=2 is an explicit extension that halves alpha while retaining the fixed direction toward lower experimental hazard.

remaining: Native automatic inverse bounds and branch discovery; discrete significance planning by critical-region selection; integer allocation of proportional K-group totals; joint historical-control accrual-time/allocation optimization.
Alternative exponential and piecewise-survival curve parameter conversions.
Legacy matched-pairs option ampd, commented out of the current main menu.

planning_reference.reproduction: Compile the listed original files in order with the repository harness in an empty directory, using the listed flags. Run the executable. Retain the CSV header and seven six-column rows; qcor1 also prints a non-CSV diagnostic line. Original archive must be acquired separately.
planning_reference.independent_runtime: R 4.4.1, base and stats packages only
planning_reference.independent_method: Independent forward formulas evaluated with R distributions, finite sums and adaptive quadrature; uniroot for continuous parameters and bounded enumeration for integer attainment, across all 25 STPLAN forward procedures.
native_differences: qnor1 effect and SD inversion use sums of central-t quantiles. In the retained example target power 0.8 gives actual noncentral-t power 0.804990987754303. Python solves the forward power equation instead.
Native inverse routines use their original quantile and root-finding tolerances. Valid sample-size and significance reference roots are compared with tolerance for these solvers.

survival_input_reference.independent_method: Base R linear systems in cumulative-hazard space; covers both known-breakpoint branches, inferred breakpoints, zero and equal hazards, subnormal survival, and time rescaling.
survival_input_reference.source_documentation: STPLAN user manual chapter 26 (two-hazard curve specifications) and chapter 25 (historical-control input options).

historical_allocation_reference.native_method: qschc option 7, using foschc to invert accrual duration and funmax to optimize control allocation. pschc independently re-evaluates returned designs. Two cases reproduce user manual chapters 25.4 and 25.5.
historical_allocation_reference.native_reproduction: Compile the listed files, in order, from the separately downloaded STPLAN 4.5 SOURCE directory with the listed flags and the native harness. Run the resulting probe and retain the CSV header and six data rows.
historical_allocation_reference.independent_method: Base R Dixon-Simon normal approximation, stable uniform-accrual expected events, uniroot duration solutions, and allocation search with a 129-point scan plus local refinement and explicit endpoints. Includes a constrained allocation minimum.
historical_allocation_reference.native_comparison: All six original outputs agree with independent R within 1e-8 relative duration and 2e-8 absolute allocation (or 1e-6 relative allocation).
